title: Gambas al Ajillo
subtitle: Prawns cooked fast in olive oil, garlic and dried chilli
excerpt: Large raw prawns sizzled in plenty of garlicky olive oil with dried chilli, served bubbling hot straight from the pan.
sourceNotes: A Spanish tapas classic, traditionally cooked and served in individual clay dishes called cazuelas.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Peel and devein the prawns up to a day ahead and keep refrigerated.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Spanish cooking style where ingredients are cooked quickly in olive oil with garlic and dried chilli.

content.text: This recipe serves 4 as a tapas dish and cooks in under 10 minutes once everything is prepped. The entire dish is defined by timing: the garlic must golden without burning, and the prawns must be pulled from the heat the moment they turn pink and curl.

Have everything ready before the pan goes on the heat. This is not a dish you can prepare while it cooks. Slice the garlic, measure the oil, pat the prawns dry, and have a plate ready to transfer to. Once the heat is on, the whole thing takes less than 8 minutes.

items.prepNote: large, peeled and deveined, tails on

content.text: Pat the prawns completely dry with kitchen paper. Season lightly with black pepper.

Pour the olive oil into a 26cm frying pan and add the garlic and dried chilli. Set over a medium heat and cook gently for 2 to 3 minutes, watching carefully, until the garlic is golden and fragrant. Do not let it burn.
Turn the heat to high. Add the prawns in a single layer and cook for 1 to 2 minutes without moving until the undersides are pink.
Flip each prawn and cook for 1 minute more until just cooked through and curled. Remove from the heat immediately.
Scatter over the parsley and serve straight from the pan, or transfer to a warm dish. Put lemon wedges on the side and plenty of bread to soak up the oil.

items.problem: The garlic burnt before the prawns went in
items.solution: Keep the heat at medium when frying the garlic. It should sizzle gently, not aggressively. If it burns, start again with fresh oil.

items.problem: The prawns are rubbery and overcooked
items.solution: Prawns cook in less than 3 minutes total. Pull them off the heat as soon as they are fully pink and curled into a C shape.

items.problem: The oil spat everywhere during cooking
items.solution: The prawns had too much surface moisture. Pat them as dry as possible before they go into the pan.

content.text: is found in tapas bars from Seville to San Sebastian, usually served in a clay cazuela kept sizzling on a small gas burner at the table. The olive oil left in the pan is half the point: use it to dip bread. It is a dish that asks for nothing beyond good prawns, good oil, and a little heat.
